name: Decorative tags and status pills
summary: Show a tag only when users filter, group or act on it; drop it or write plain metadata for everything else.
problem: Rows of coloured, bordered pills turn information that needs no emphasis into visual noise. Status chips such as "Automatically saved" tell users nothing they can use.

bad.description: Four coloured, bordered pills on one title: Automatically saved, Draft, Updated 2m ago, Private.

good.title: Plain metadata
good.description: One muted line of text. Nothing to scan, nothing to colour.

good.title: Functional tag
good.description: A neutral Tag (one background, no border) for a category that users really filter and group by.

good.title: Notification
good.description: An event such as a save is acknowledged briefly in a notification instead of a permanent badge.

why: Plain text is quieter and quicker to read. Reserving tags for functional categories means that when one appears, users know it can be used.
exceptions: Tags are allowed when they are a functional filter, category or state that users recognise, filter or interact with (labels, issue status in a tracker, stock tickers).
A failure state that users must notice and fix (for example "Not saved") may use a tag or an inline indicator.

humanReview: Could a user filter, group or click this tag?
Would removing the tag reduce comprehension?
